findings.title: Path traversal prevention in sample upload filename sanitization
findings.attack_preconditions: Attacker submits malicious filename with '../' or backslashes in multipart header
findings.impact: Storage path traversal or directory escaping if filename was used directly
findings.evidence: sanitize_filename strips all path elements via Path.name and safe regex character substitution, and storage paths use content-addressed SHA256 hashes
findings.root_cause: Untrusted filename header supplied in multipart upload
findings.remediation: Strict filename sanitization and content-addressed storage isolation using SHA256 hash digests
findings.residual_risk: None for storage; original filename is retained strictly as metadata string

findings.title: Resource exhaustion via unbounded upload stream
findings.attack_preconditions: Attacker streams arbitrary multi-gigabyte payload in upload body
findings.impact: Host disk space and memory exhaustion
findings.evidence: Streaming chunk loop checks size_bytes > max_upload_bytes on every 64KB chunk and immediately aborts with HTTP 413 and deletes temporary file
findings.root_cause: Unbounded HTTP stream ingestion without chunk-level limit enforcement
findings.remediation: Stream in 64KB chunks with strict size enforcement and exception-guaranteed temporary file cleanup
findings.residual_risk: Low; max_upload_bytes default is 50MB, configurable via IGRIS_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES

findings.title: Missing defensive HTTP response security headers
findings.attack_preconditions: Browser client accessing API in cross-origin or framing context
findings.impact: MIME-type sniffing or iframe clickjacking in browser contexts
findings.evidence: SecurityHeadersMiddleware enforces X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, CSP, and Referrer-Policy
findings.root_cause: FastAPI default does not include explicit security headers
findings.remediation: Added ASGI middleware enforcing strict headers across all responses

findings.title: PDF content stream delimiter injection via unescaped string literals
findings.attack_preconditions: Hostile sample or analyst notes containing unbalanced parentheses or backslashes
findings.attacker_controlled_input: Hostile strings in sample metadata or analyst notes
findings.impact: PDF syntax corruption or viewer parsing failure
findings.evidence: _sanitize_pdf_text escapes backslashes and parentheses and strips control characters
findings.root_cause: Direct insertion of arbitrary UTF-8 strings into PDF content stream
findings.remediation: Implement strict PDF string escaping, control character stripping, and safe Type 1 font encoding
findings.residual_risk: None; PDF renderer runs purely in-memory without invoking external binaries

residual_risks: Single-Tenant Research Assumption: Igris is currently designed as a single-tenant local/research platform and does not implement multi-user RBAC or OAuth2/OIDC authentication.

Emulated Behavioral Sandbox: Behavioral analysis in default test configurations uses synthetic/emulated telemetry; production deployment with live malware execution requires external hardware-isolated hypervisor VMs.
Binary Parser Memory Bounds: While Python memory safety prevents buffer overflows, extremely large binaries are bounded by max_upload_bytes (50MB default).
deployment_assumptions: Igris API is hosted within a secure internal network or isolated analyst workstation.
Direct network exposure of the API to untrusted public networks requires a reverse proxy (e.g. Nginx, Envoy) with TLS termination and external authentication.
Storage directories (data/samples, data/metadata) are mounted with restricted read/write permissions for the Igris process user.
overall_assessment: SECURITY REVIEW COMPLETE — HARDENED WITH DOCUMENTED RESIDUAL RISK
